Class ChaosQuarkusExtension

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.quarkus.ChaosQuarkusExtension
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterTestExecutionCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeTestExecutionCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.Extension, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ParameterResolver
public final class ChaosQuarkusExtension extends Object implements org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeTestExecutionCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterTestExecutionCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ParameterResolver
JUnit 5 extension that installs the chaos agent once per test JVM and opens a class-scoped ChaosSession for Quarkus-based tests.

Installed automatically by QuarkusChaosTest, or directly via @ExtendWith(ChaosQuarkusExtension.class) on any JUnit test class.

Lifecycle

  • beforeAll: self-attach the agent (idempotent), open one session for the whole test class, and activate every ChaosScenario annotation present on the class. A @Nested class runs inside its outer class and shares its session. The opening thread is unbound again at once (bindSession(null)), so an application Quarkus starts on that thread after this callback (when @QuarkusTest is registered after this extension, or for a @Nested class with a test profile of its own) starts outside the session: a long-lived thread it starts (an event loop, a consumer, a worker loop) serves the whole application, not the class that happened to start it.
  • beforeEach / afterEach: bind the thread that runs the test to the class's session, so the test's @BeforeEach methods, the test method and its @AfterEach methods run in it. Quarkus runs the test and lifecycle methods itself and skips the rest of the invocation chain, so the binding is made by these callbacks, not by an InvocationInterceptor; @BeforeAll and @AfterAll methods run outside the session.
  • beforeTestExecution: activate every ChaosScenario and WithChaos annotation present on the test method, right before the test method runs (after its @BeforeEach methods). The activations of either scope are tracked per method so afterTestExecution can tear them down — otherwise the second test method that declared the same scenario id would hit an "already active" activation conflict.
  • afterTestExecution: stop the scenarios activated by the current method's annotations, right after the test method ran (before its @AfterEach methods); class-level scenarios remain active for the whole class.
  • afterAll: stop the scenarios activated by class-level annotations and close the session (which stops every session-scoped scenario activated during the class).

Parameter injection

The extension injects ChaosSession and ChaosControlPlane parameters on test methods and lifecycle methods. Constructor parameters are left to Quarkus' own extension, which resolves every one of them (a ChaosControlPlane there is the CDI bean).

  • Method Details

    • contextPlane

      @Internal public static ChaosControlPlane contextPlane(ChaosControlPlane delegate)
      Returns a tracking control plane for the application's bean, released when the application stops or when the last running chaos test class ends. Only what it activated is released: the application's event listeners and sessions stay. Called by ChaosArcProducer in a test, through the system class loader that loaded this extension; not for application code.
      Parameters:
      delegate - the JVM-wide control plane
      Returns:
      the tracking control plane

    • releaseContextPlane

      @Internal public static void releaseContextPlane(ChaosControlPlane plane)
      Releases a plane contextPlane(ChaosControlPlane) returned when its application stops: what it activated stops, and it is no longer released with the others. Called by ChaosArcProducer; not for application code.
      Parameters:
      plane - the plane being released
